page.layout: One page of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Top: running head and page number. Bottom centre: gathering signature. No text in the left margin, only a dark smudge.

main_text.p: duobus suffultus{a} dæmonibus evolasset,dæmoni- is.Paris[?]. orationibus apostolorum fugatis dæmo-nibus, delapsus in terram, populo inspe-ctate, diruptus est. Interea abundate jam Christianorum multitudine, accidit ut Roma incendio conflagraret, Neronea-pud Antiu constituto. Sed opinio omni-um invidiam incedii in principem retor-quebat, credebaturq; imperator gloriam innovandæ urbis quæsisse. Neque ulla re Nero efficiebat, quin ab eo jussum incen-dium putaretur. Igitur vertit invidiam in Christianos, actaeque in innoxios crude-lissimæ quæstiones: quin & novæ mortes excogitatæ, ut ferarum tergis contecti, la-niatu canum interirent. Multi crucibusCorn.Ta-citus l.15. affixi, aut flamma usti. Pleriq; in id reser-ati, ut cum defecifler dies, in usum no-curni luminis urerentur. Hoc initio inAn.Chri-sti 68. Christianos sæviri coeptum. Posteriam {b}datis legibus religio vetabatur: palamq;latis. edistis propositis, Christianum esse nonSig. licebat. Tum Paulus ac Petrus capitisDion.Y.r. Corinth. epistol. damnati: quorum uni cervix gladio de-secta, Petrus in crucem sublatus est. DumEuseb.l.2. ca.35 & 36.hist. hæc Romæ geruntur, Iudæi, præsidis sui {c}Festi Flori injurias non ferentes, rebel-eccl. c Cessij leg exlof.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right are transcribed in place; several are partly worn and their letters, especially in the Eusebius and Dionysius references, are uncertain. The mark "c" at "Festi" is read from a small mark at the line start. The left margin carries only a dark smudge and no text. The bottom-right ornament is not printed text. The final line ends with "rebel-" and continues on the next page.
